secciones.narrativa_beneficiario: Payment description visible in bank statement
secciones.notas: ACH is the most common method for receiving payments in the US. Same-day ACH available for faster settlement.

secciones.canales: All US banks with Fedwire access
secciones.narrativa_beneficiario: Full sender details and reference included
secciones.notas: Wire transfers are faster but more expensive than ACH. Best for high-value transactions.
FedNow is the US instant payment system launched in 2023. Available 24/7/365.
Card payments have higher fees but instant authorization. Subject to chargebacks.
SPEI is the primary real-time payment system in Mexico. Available 24/7/365.
Popular for customers without bank accounts. Requires generating payment reference.
Card payments in Mexico require 3D Secure authentication. Support for monthly installments (Meses Sin Intereses).

datos_obligatorios: PIX Key (CPF, CNPJ, Email, Phone, or Random Key)
secciones.notas: PIX is the dominant payment method in Brazil. Launched in 2020 and now has 150M+ users. Available 24/7/365.

secciones.canales: Banks, lottery shops, convenience stores, online
secciones.notas: Traditional payment method in Brazil. Good for customers without cards. Can be paid in cash or via bank transfer.
TED is being replaced by PIX but still used for large business transfers. Higher fees than PIX.
Brazilian cards support installment payments (parcelado). Common to split payments up to 12x.
PSE is the most popular online payment method in Colombia. Direct bank debit with instant authorization.
ACH Colombia processes transactions in 5 daily cycles. Used for business transfers.

secciones.canales: Efecty, Baloto, Su Red, bank branches
secciones.notas: Cash payments through correspondent banking agents. Popular in regions with low banking penetration.
Nequi and Daviplata are the leading digital wallets in Colombia. Mobile-first payment experience.
Card payments in Colombia support installments (cuotas). 3D Secure authentication required.
Transferencia 3.0 is Argentina's instant payment system. Available 24/7 using CBU, CVU, or Alias.
DEBIN requires customer to actively authorize payment through their bank app. Popular for e-commerce.
Mercado Pago is the leading digital wallet in Argentina with 40M+ users. Integrated with e-commerce.
Argentine cards support extensive installment plans (up to 18 cuotas). Local cards (Cabal, Naranja) widely used.
TEF (Transferencia Electrónica de Fondos) is the standard for bank transfers in Chile.
Webpay is the dominant payment gateway in Chile. Supports credit, debit, and prepaid cards.

secciones.canales: Banco Pichincha, Banco Guayaquil, Produbanco, Banco Pacífico, etc.
secciones.notas: Bank transfers are the preferred payment method by 57% of Ecuadorians. Ecuador uses USD as official currency.
PayPhone is Ecuador's leading mobile payment platform. Supports QR code payments and phone-to-phone transfers.

secciones.red_participante: Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Diners Club
secciones.notas: Card payments widely accepted in Ecuador. Diners Club is particularly popular. 3D Secure authentication required.
Cash payments used by 32% of Ecuadorians. Popular for customers without bank accounts.
CCI (Código de Cuenta Interbancario) is the standard account identifier for interbank transfers in Peru.
Yape and Plin are the leading mobile payment apps in Peru. QR code payments supported.
Bank transfers are the most common payment method in Uruguay. High banking penetration.
OCA is Uruguay's local card brand. Installment payments common.
Panama uses both USD and PAB (Balboa) interchangeably at 1:1. ACH is the standard for electronic transfers.
Yappy is Panama's leading mobile payment app. Very popular for P2P and merchant payments.
Card usage is very high in Panama. No installment payments common.

secciones.canales: All Costa Rican banks and mobile apps
secciones.notas: SINPE Móvil is Costa Rica's instant payment system. Very popular and widely adopted. Uses phone numbers as identifiers.
Costa Rica supports both CRC and USD accounts. IBAN format used for account numbers.
Card payments support both CRC and USD. Installments common.

secciones.canales: Banco Popular, BHD León, Banreservas, Banco BDI
secciones.notas: Bank transfers available in both DOP (Dominican Peso) and USD.
Card payments widely accepted. Both DOP and USD supported.

secciones.canales: All major banks and UPI apps (Google Pay, PhonePe, Paytm, etc.)
secciones.notas: UPI is the most popular payment method in India with 10B+ transactions/month. Supports QR codes and deep linking.
NEFT processes transactions in hourly batches. Available 24/7 since Dec 2019.
IMPS is faster than NEFT but has transaction limits. Available 24/7.

secciones.canales: All banks in SEPA zone (36 countries)
secciones.notas: SEPA is the standard for euro transfers within Europe. SEPA Instant available for real-time payments.
SEPA Instant provides real-time euro transfers. Available 24/7/365. €100,000 limit per transaction.
SEPA Direct Debit requires pre-authorized mandate from customer. Good for recurring payments.
